case.paper_title: Human Capital and Development Accounting: New Evidence from Wage Gains at Migration
case.focal_claim: ... immigrants who have never been to high school gain ... more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree (p. 682.)
case.hypothesis: Among immigrants from poor countries, the proportional wage gain at migration (log of U.S. adjusted wage minus log of home adjusted wage) is larger for immigrants who never attended high school (edyrs < 9) than for immigrants with a college degree (edyrs ≥ 16).

tasks_info.task_instruction: Conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: Use the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the NIS and the Migration Projects, including Mexico. Do not control for sector: agriculture/nonagriculture, and region i.e. whether an immigrant grew up in a rural or an urban area.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

datasets.source_type: Survey-based wage histories (NIS; Mexican and Latin American Migration Projects), pooled and preprocessed into a wage gain table.
datasets.wave_or_subset: Pooled poor-country immigrant sample including Mexico, with PPP/price-adjusted hourly wages and demographic fields.
datasets.notes: Dataset wage variables are strongly right-skewed with extreme values; analysis uses log transformation of adjusted wages. Columns are complete (no missing) but constructed outcomes will drop rows with non-positive wages. Sex coded 1=male, 2=female. Education years span 0–20.

plan.path_summary: Construct log wage gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), classify education into never-high-school (edyrs<9) vs college-degree (edyrs≥16), restrict to positive adjusted wages, and estimate education differences in proportional wage gains. Task1 uses OLS with demographic, country, and cohort fixed effects and HC3 robust SEs. Task2, per constraints, excludes sector and region controls and uses OLS with only demographic controls.

path_signature.controls: Task-specific; see tasks. No sector/rural variables used in any task.
path_signature.sample_restriction: Positive adjusted wages; restrict to focal education groups.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on material variables (outcome, edu_group, demographics, FE variables).
path_signature.inference_rule: Support for claim if the coefficient on never_high_school (relative to college_degree) is positive with p < 0.05.

analysis_path.path_description: Estimate OLS of log wage gain on education group with controls for female, age and age^2, country fixed effects, and birth-cohort (decade) fixed effects; use HC3 robust SEs.
preprocessing_steps: Coerce numeric columns: edyrs, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, sex, yrborn, lastHomeWage, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWage, lastUsWageAdjusted.
Require lastHomeWageAdjusted > 0 and lastUsWageAdjusted > 0; drop others.
Construct female = 1 if sex == 2, else 0 if sex == 1.
Define edu_group = never_high_school if edyrs < 9; college_degree if edyrs >= 16; other otherwise.
Create cohort_decade = floor(yrborn/10)*10 as a factor label (e.g., '1960s').
Drop rows with missing material variables (outcome, female, age_at_us_job, edu_group, country, cohort_decade).
Restrict to focal education groups (college_degree, never_high_school) and set college_degree as reference.

key_choices.outcome_measure: Proportional wage gain on migration, via log differences.
key_choices.main_predictor_measure: Education group indicator: never_high_school (edyrs<9) vs college_degree (edyrs≥16).
key_choices.sample_restriction: Positive adjusted wages; focal education groups only.
key_choices.outlier_rule: No explicit trimming; rely on log scale to mitigate extreme values.
key_choices.data_processing: Variable construction as above; no weighting.
key_choices.inference_rule: Coefficient on never_high_school > 0 with p < 0.05 indicates support.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ edu_group + female + age_at_us_job + I(age_at_us_job^2) + factor(country) + factor(cohort_decade)
models.planned_estimation: Coefficient on edu_groupnever_high_school relative to college_degree; report robust SE (HC3), p-value, 95% CI, and percent difference 100*(exp(beta)-1).
models.inference_criteria: Positive coefficient with p < 0.05 supports the claim.
models.qualification: Adds cohort fixed effects and HC3 robust SEs, which is a valid extension under 'no restrictions' and differs from prior paths that did not include cohort FE or used clustering.

outcome.name: log_wage_gain
outcome.definition: Difference between log of PPP/price-adjusted U.S. hourly wage and log of PPP/price-adjusted home-country hourly wage for the last pre- and post-migration jobs.
outcome.variable_construction: log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), requiring both adjusted wages > 0.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Drop non-positive or non-finite wage observations.
outcome.qualification: Proportional wage gains directly align with the paper’s presentation of migration gains.

main_predictor.name: edu_group
main_predictor.definition: Education group comparing immigrants who have never been to high school (edyrs < 9) with immigrants holding a college degree (edyrs ≥ 16).
main_predictor.variable_construction: Factor with levels {college_degree, never_high_school, other}, then restrict to the first two and set college_degree as reference.
main_predictor.missing_data_handling: Drop rows outside focal groups or with missing edyrs.
main_predictor.qualification: Matches the focal claim’s contrast exactly.

controls.name: female
controls.definition: Indicator for female (1) vs male (0) based on sex code in dataset.
controls.variable_construction: female = 1 if sex == 2, else 0 if sex == 1.
controls.missing_data_handling: Drop rows with undefined sex codes.
controls.qualification: Adjusts for gender composition differences in wages.

controls.name: age_at_us_job
controls.definition: Age at last U.S. job, proxy for labor market experience.
controls.qualification: Controls for lifecycle/experience effects on wages.

controls.name: I(age_at_us_job^2)
controls.definition: Quadratic age term to allow nonlinear wage-age profile.
controls.variable_construction: Square of age_at_us_job in model formula.
controls.qualification: Standard to capture curvature in age-earnings profiles.

controls.name: factor(country)
controls.definition: Country fixed effects for source country.
controls.variable_construction: Treat country as a categorical factor.
controls.qualification: Adjusts for compositional differences across origin countries.

controls.name: factor(cohort_decade)
controls.qualification: Controls for cohort differences and aligns with paper’s attention to arrival and cohort robustness; differs from prior paths.

expected_outputs: Sample flow counts (starting, removed by rule, final).
OLS coefficient table with HC3 robust SEs.
Focal coefficient (never_high_school vs college_degree), robust SE, t, p, 95% CI, and percent difference.

estimand.quantity: Coefficient difference in mean log wage gain between never-high-school and college-degree immigrants, conditional on controls.
estimand.outcome_scale: log units (interpretable as percentage difference via exp(coef)-1).
estimand.target_population: Immigrants in the pooled poor-country sample (including Mexico) meeting positivity and focal-group criteria.
estimand.time_scope: Last home-country job versus last U.S. job (cross-sectional difference at migration).
estimand.claim_mapping: Directly tests whether less educated immigrants have larger proportional wage gains than college graduates at migration.

tasks.notes_for_agent: Use demographic-only controls; do not include sector or rural/urban region controls, and do not add country fixed effects.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Both tasks estimate the proportional wage gain difference (log-wage difference) between never-high-school and college-degree immigrants, directly addressing the stated focal claim.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Uses only the authorized pooled wage_gain_table.xlsx with PPP/price-adjusted hourly wages and demographic fields.
method_justification.method_reason: Log differences appropriately handle wage scale and skewness and yield interpretable percent differences. Task1 adds fixed effects for country and birth cohort with HC3 SEs under the no-restriction rule; Task2 respects the instruction to exclude sector/region by using demographic-only controls.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Task1 differs from prior paths by including cohort fixed effects and HC3 robust SEs (no clustering), while Task2 differs by using demographic-only controls without country fixed effects, satisfying constraints and avoiding prior bivariate or country-FE models.

self_check.self_check_note: Variables verified in dataset; code reflects declared models and constraints; both tasks differ from paths in shared memory.
